title: Performance Composer: Model & Route Mosaic with Cost Overlay
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Produce a handoff-ready design and interactive prototype for a unified Performance Composer that lets engineers and product teams compare models and routes side-by-side, inspect latency distributions, throughput trends, and token-cost attribution. This ticket covers: design exploration, chart spec definitions, a clickable Figma prototype for desktop/tablet, and a short walkthrough video for PM/Eng review. Context: existing Console has many per-route tiles but lacks a compact, comparative surface that overlays cost signals with latency and token flow. Scope: mosaic grid of route/model tiles, timeline strip, latency distribution panel, token flow waterfall, and a cost overlay toggle. Out of scope: server-side instrumentation changes and backend schema updates (handled in ENG-3012).
acceptance_criteria: Figma files with desktop and tablet frames, responsive behavior notes, and component variants checked in.

Interactive prototype that demonstrates: 1) comparing 3 models across the same route, 2) switching grouping between model-first and route-first, 3) toggling cost overlay, and 4) drilling into a token waterfall for a sampled request.
Chart spec doc listing each chart (series names, aggregation method, recommended time windows: 1m/1h/24h/7d, default percentile markers, and example datasets).
Handoff pack: color tokens, spacing scale, typography, exportable SVGs/PNGs for icons, and a short written handover for ENG with noted interactions and accessibility constraints.
Sign-off from PM (Leo Martinez) and Lead Eng (Sana Kulkarni) recorded in comments.
design_notes: Primary canvas: 3-up mosaic (model tiles vs route tiles) where each tile contains sparkline throughput, median latency, and token-per-request indicator.
Tile expand behavior: expand to show full timeline + latency violin + top failure reasons and a compact cost bar (per-token cost line + total cost area).
Timeline strip: global time selector + commit/rollout markers; hovering shows synced crosshair across tiles.

Token waterfall: when drilling into sampled traces, show prompt tokens, model-generated tokens, KV cache hits annotated; include estimated per-token cost overlay with a toggle to show raw vs normalized cost.
Normalization: allow per-1000-token normalization and per-request normalization (useful for bursty routes).
Legend and filtering: support filtering by model variant, region, and customer tier; persist filters in URL for shareable links.
Accessibility: ensure color palette meets 4.5:1 contrast for primary chart lines and provide patterned fills for area charts to avoid color-only encodings.
Performance constraints: charts must render within Console budget (initial render <= 250ms with summary data); heavy traces load lazily with a spinner.
Design tokens: use existing console token scale (redwood:spacing-2/3/4, typography-scale) and reference runtime-1.20 compatible color variables.
decisions: Use small-multiples mosaic (3 columns default) rather than a single dense table to preserve visual pattern recognition across models and routes.
Latency distribution to be a compact violin when tile is expanded and a median-plus-percentiles microwidget when collapsed.
Cost overlay will be an optional layer (on/off) and default to off for new users to avoid cognitive overload.
Streaming/real-time indicator will appear as a pulsing dot and not change chart aggregation behavior; real-time traces can be toggled to a live tail mode.
Use 50th/90th/99th percentile markers as the default percentile set; make percentiles configurable in settings.
